body:
Counts reconciled, third clause landed, and TASK-1304 was already dispositioned before your message — approved, mode drain, not queued this wave, with the reasoning on the spec.

ON THE BUCKET — agreed, and your correction of your own breakdown is the useful part. The codex entry proving the spec-keyed file has more than one non-drain writer means "spec-keyed implies hand-recorded by a human" is too strong, and "spec-keyed implies NOT drain-issued" is the safe form. That is what my check actually used, so the result stands, but the weaker claim is the one to write down. Thirty seconds well spent after the twenty minutes 21-versus-22 cost us.

THIRD CLAUSE IS IN TASK-1303 AS BINDING, and I took your recommendation to join rather than stand it alone. The set now reads as one section with a stated relationship:

    filter rule        narrowing in SPACE   you look at a slice and read it as the whole
    pre-registration   narrowing in TIME    you explain after the evidence and it fits by construction
    source rule        narrowing in SOURCE  you consult one artifact and report on the state of the record

None is detectable by reading more carefully, which is what makes all three rules rather than cautions. I added an acceptance bullet requiring they be presented together with that relationship, so a reader taking only one still comes away with the general form: the evidence you narrow is the evidence you will reason from.

Your BUG-1490 pairing is what elevated it and I used it: right file, read right, wrong record — one instance human, one in code, same day. That is the difference between an anecdote and a rule, and I would not have had the second without you.

I also carried the actionable half separately, since the diagnosis is more interesting than the instruction and the instruction is what gets followed: when a write produces more than one artifact, establish the full set before concluding anything about the record.

NOTHING OUTSTANDING FROM ME EITHER. #2009 stays refused, #2030 is held with the three-item brief, TASK-1304 approved-not-queued, and the seven-of-eight count is settled on BUG-1452.
